name: Forced Flight
description: Flight matching Palladium's default movement and animation, except the entity can never land or toggle out. It only stops when the granting ability is disabled.

fields.description: The normal flight speed.
The sprinting flight speed, defaulting to the normal speed when unset.
Camera shake while sprinting in flight. Only used when a sprint_speed is set.
Looping sound played while fast-flying (sprinting), its volume scaling with flight speed.

name: Default Flight
description: Default flying type. If the sprint speed is equal or less than the normal speed, this flight will be levitation-only.

fields.description: The normal flight speed.
The sprinting flight speed. If not set, it will be equal to the normal speed.
Screen shake applied while the entity is in propelled flight.
Looping sound played constantly while flying. If propelled_sound is set as well, the two sounds fade between each other depending on whether the entity is in propelled flight.
Looping sound played while the entity is fast-flying (sprinting). Volume scales with flight speed.
Sound played once when the entity enters propelled flight.

If enabled, the entity starts flying as soon as the flight ability is enabled and can't stop on its own. Double jumping and touching the ground won't end the flight, only disabling the ability or getting into a vehicle does.

name: Swinging
description: Allows the entity to swing from anchor points, similar to a grappling hook.

fields.description: The maximum height for anchor points.
Determines if the maximum height for anchors are relative to the ground, or a fixed y-level.

The web length range: how far ahead anchors are placed and the maximum rope length. A single number or an array of 2 numbers (min/max). While flying, holding jump raises and holding shift lowers the height that new anchors are placed at.
The airborne gap (in ticks) between releasing one web and firing the next. The first web after starting the flight always fires at the apex of the launch boost.
The beam renderer(s) used for the swinging rope. Can be a single identifier or separate right/left arm identifiers.
Sound played for nearby players each time a new anchor attaches.
Looping sound played while the entity is swinging on an anchor. Volume scales with movement speed.

name: Controlled Flight
description: Flight with momentum, banking and a body that leans into its travel direction. Speed still comes from "speed" and "sprint_speed". Toggling, speed levels, landing and takeoff work like palladium:flight.

fields.description: The normal flight speed.
The sprinting (propelled) flight speed. Unset, sprinting does nothing special.

Presets every setting below: controlled is the balanced default, propelled has heavier momentum and sinks when no direction is held, natural turns and stops quickly with no gravity, gliding keeps momentum and sinks when slow.
Screen shake while propelled.
Ambient flight sound.
Looping sound while propelled.
Sound played once when propelled flight starts.
Fraction of the gap to the target speed closed each tick when speeding up (0.001 to 1).
Fraction of the gap closed each tick when slowing down while a direction is held (0.001 to 1).
Shapes acceleration over speed. 1 is constant, above 1 starts slower and pushes harder near top speed (0.1 to 4).
How much turning is held back at speed. 0 turns as sharply at speed as when slow, 1 holds the heading the most.
The heading change in degrees per tick when turning at low speed.
Fraction of speed lost each tick when no direction is held (0 to 1).
How much gravity pulls while no direction is held, or always for the gliding profile, where it fades as speed rises (0 to 1).
Gliding profile only. How much speed is traded for height. Dropping adds speed, climbing costs it (0 to 0.3).
Gliding profile only. The fraction of top speed at which gravity is fully cancelled. Slower than this the player sinks (0.05 to 1).
Extra fraction of speed removed each tick when almost stopped, so the player settles into a hover.
Speed below which hover stabilization starts, scaled by 3.
Whether the player's body leans into the direction of travel while flying.
Fraction of top speed at which the lean begins.
Fraction of top speed at which the body is fully aligned with the direction of travel.
How quickly the body follows the direction of travel each tick.
Whether the body rolls into turns.
The largest bank angle in degrees.
How quickly the bank builds each tick.
How quickly the bank returns to level each tick.
How much the bank scales with speed, 0 banks the same at any speed.
How much of the bank the camera follows.
The share of the bank the camera rolls by in partial mode.
Whether the field of view widens with flight speed.
How much the field of view widens at top speed.
Whether the third person camera frames the body while flying, so the character stays near the middle of the screen however the body leans. First person is unchanged.
How far above the middle of the body the third person camera aims, in blocks. Positive puts the character a little below the screen middle, 0 puts the body center on it (-1 to 2).
Whether double-tapping left or right while flying does a barrel roll that way. Off by default.
How many ticks the roll takes.
A sideways push in the roll direction, as a fraction of top speed.
Ticks before another roll can start.
How much of the roll the camera follows, 0 keeps the view steady and 1 rolls with the body.
The fraction of top speed needed to start a roll.
Whether hitting a block or an entity at speed hurts. Off by default.
Multiplier on damage from hitting a block, worked out from the impact speed like elytra damage.
Multiplier on the damage dealt to an entity that is flown into.
How hard a hit entity is knocked away.
Whether an impact stops the player's speed.
The impact speed in blocks per tick below which a collision does nothing.

Whether gravity turns with the flight so loops and vertical flight have no pitch limit. Past gravity_wrap_pitch it turns 90 degrees about the player's right side and goes back to normal when flight ends.
How steeply the player has to be flying up or down, in degrees (30 to 80), before gravity turns.
How many ticks the camera and model take to turn with gravity.

Whether flight lands by itself when dropping toward the ground: soft touchdown, upright body, stop after the recovery time and no fall damage. Faster than landing_speed_threshold is a hard landing instead.
The downward speed, in blocks per tick, up to which a landing is controlled. Faster than this the flight doesn't brake and touching the ground is a hard landing.
Ticks of recovery on the ground before flight stops after a landing. Moving cancels it early.
How much fall damage from a hard landing is prevented (0 to 1). It is dealt as fall damage, so Palladium's fall protection still applies.

Whether looking steeply down while pushing forward is a dive. A dive can reach dive_acceleration_multiplier times top speed and the extra speed fades slowly, so pulling out keeps momentum. There is no key, it follows the look direction.
How far down the player must look, in degrees (30 to 85), for a dive to start. It builds to full at 85.
The top speed of a full dive as a multiple of the normal top speed (1 to 4).
How much extra dive speed carries on after the dive. 0 loses it at the normal deceleration, 1 loses it at dive_momentum_decay.
The fraction of extra dive speed lost each tick at full retention (0.001 to 0.3). The extra speed never lets the player pass the dive speed and always fades.
How much easier turning is above top speed, so pulling out of a dive doesn't need a huge circle (1 to 4).
